title: Fort Victoria, British Columbia

buildingCutout.basis: The documented fort courtyard, limited to its historical viewing period.

terrainReference.basis: Sample the source elevation on the former principal courtyard route near Fort Street. The 1860 forecourt and individual footing elevations are inferred separately.

mapIdentity.provider: Native OpenStreetMap street intersections and plaques, City of Victoria commemorative brick trace, Maritime Museum site walk and Fawcett’s 1859 eyewitness account.
mapIdentity.scope: The historical east gate follows Fort Street on Government Street, and the west gate follows the same line toward Wharf Street. City survey and commemorative brickwork tie the northern palisade and northeast bastion to Government and Bastion Square. The southwest bastion is inside the present Broughton and Wharf corner. Fawcett’s eyewitness text and the Maritime Museum tour support reconstruction of a nearly rectangular enclosure inside the four modern streets. The width is an estimate from the street and marker alignment, with the north–south extent close to the roughly 465 feet described after the 1847 enlargement.

note: The exact September 1860 Crease watercolor and contemporary published copy establish the southwest octagonal bastion and stockade. Five original illustrations published in Fawcett’s 1912 eyewitness memoir show the same bastion, different north and east views, both the whitewashed hipped buildings and the bell tower and gate facing Fort Street. Fawcett places offices and residences east, stores north, barns south and the bell tower in the yard. Earlier reports and construction notes provide typical scales and materials.
